cvEn:
Benyamin Kamri, son of Ayala and Seadya, was born on 14 Iyar 5712 (9 May 1952) in Rehovot. He studied at the Moriah elementary school and at the Air Force technical school, within the framework of Shahar-IDF, and through this framework he completed basic training. In June 1970 he enlisted and served in the Air Force. He completed a series of professional courses, and at the end of 1970 he was promoted to Corporal. In September 1972 he completed an advanced course as an aircraft technician and was promoted to Sergeant. His commanders gave their assessment of him: "He is a professional of good standard, disciplined, and shows initiative beyond what is required of him. He fulfills his role to the full satisfaction of his commanders."

Benyamin was a talented young man and contributed much to the spirit of his unit. He organized parties, prepared plays, and sang and played the guitar. Benyamin also wrote children's songs, studied voice development, and even composed music for some of his songs. Upon completing his regular service, he volunteered to serve in the career army as a technician in the Air Force. In the Yom Kippur War he fought with the rank of Staff Sergeant. In August 1975 he was discharged from the IDF, but he continued to serve in the reserves in his profession. His commanders valued his devoted and professional work, and in 1980 he was sent to a course for aircraft ammunition inspectors. Upon completing the course, he was promoted to Sergeant First Class. When the Lebanon War broke out, he was stationed with the Northern Command and fought in Lebanon. On 2 August 1982 he traveled with a group of soldiers from his unit toward Rosh HaNikra. On the way, an accident occurred, and Benyamin was mortally wounded. For about twenty days he fought for his life, and on Sunday, 1 Tishrei 5743 (17 September 1982), he died of his wounds. He was 30 years old at his death. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Rehovot. He left behind a wife, a daughter, parents, four sisters, and a brother. The commander of his unit in Lebanon wrote in a letter of condolence to his family: "Sergeant First Class Benyamin was posted as a reservist, an ammunition inspector, and was employed in a maintenance squadron. In reserve service he performed his role in the best possible way during the Lebanon War." The commander of his squadron wrote to his family: "Sergeant First Class Benyamin was employed as an ammunition inspector in the armaments wing, and in this role he carried out his tasks in the best possible way."
